slides.heading: Non Attacking Queens
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Recursion
slides.narration: Let's solve Non Attacking Queens, a very hard recursion problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Number of ways to place n queens on an n x n board with no two attacking.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Number of ways to place n queens on an n x n board with no two attacking. Backtracking with column or diagonal bitmasks.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Place one queen per row; track used columns and both diagonals for constant-time checks.
slides.narration: Place one queen per row; track used columns and both diagonals for constant-time checks.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Backtracking row by row with sets → O(n!)
slides.narration: Trying every placement is hopeless. Backtracking one row at a time with blocked sets prunes hard; bitmasks make it very fast.

slides.heading: Approach
slides.narration: Step by step. First, recurse row by row. Second, try each free column. Third, mark column and diagonals. Fourth, count full placements.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Place row by row with bitmasks
slides.narration: Place one queen per row. Three bitmasks track blocked columns and both diagonals.

slides.heading: Worked example

lines: take lowest bit, recurse with shifted diagonals

slides.caption: Iterate over free columns
slides.narration: Free positions are the bits not blocked. Take each lowest set bit, recurse, shifting the diagonal masks for the next row.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Results
slides.narration: For four queens there are two solutions; for eight, ninety-two.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Place returns one when all rows are filled. Otherwise it loops over free bits, recursing with the column added and diagonals shifted left and right.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n factorial. Space is O of n.

bullets: Place one queen per row; track used columns and both diagonals for constant-time checks.
